2. Here is an opportunity to convince yourself that any significant property of
a field is shared by any field isomorphic to it. The point of this problem is
to write out very formal proofs until you are certain that all statements of
this sort are obvious. F\ and F2 will be two fields which are isomorphic; for 
simplicity we will denote the operations in both by + and •. Show that:
(a) If the equation x2 + 1 =0 has a solution in Fi, then it has a solution
in F2.
(b) If every polynomial equation xn + an_\ • x"_1 + • • • + flo = 0 with
ao, in F\, has a root in F\, then every polynomial equation
x” + • x"_1 + • • • + bo = 0 with bo,..., b„_} in F2 has a root in F2.
(c) If 1 + • • • + 1 (summed m times) = 0 in F\, then the same is true in F2.
(d) If F] and F2 are ordered fields (and the isomorphism f satisfies f(x)<
f(y) for x < y) and F\ is complete, then F2 is complete.
3. Let f be an isomorphism from F\ to F2 and g an isomorphism from F2
to F3. Define the function g o f from F\ to F3 by (g o f)(x) = g(f(x)).
Show that g o f is an isomorphism.
4. Suppose that F is a complete ordered field, so that there is an isomorphism f
